_meta.purpose: MEV/MAV/MRV volume landmarks per primary muscle group. Consumed by services/volumeModule.js.

definitions.mev: Minimum Effective Volume — fewest sets per week that produce measurable adaptation.
definitions.mav: Maximum Adaptive Volume — weekly set range producing optimal adaptation for most lifters.
definitions.mrv: Maximum Recoverable Volume — most sets per week the lifter can recover from before performance degrades.

_meta.units: direct sets per week (working sets; warm-up sets excluded)
_meta.provenance_note: All landmarks are highly individual and contested. Treat as heuristic starting points for an untrained estimate; the real user's tolerance emerges from logged history. Sources derive from Israetel (RP Strength), Schoenfeld, and practitioner consensus — none are controlled-trial values at this granularity.

gluteus maximus.note: Heavily recruited by squats and deadlifts as indirect volume; direct isolation optional.

triceps brachii.note: Substantial indirect volume from pressing compounds; direct sets supplement.

biceps brachii.note: Indirect volume from rows and pull-ups; direct curls supplement.

anterior deltoid.note: Heavily recruited by all horizontal and vertical pressing; rarely needs direct work.

lateral deltoid.note: Small muscle with high volume tolerance; responds to high-frequency direct work.

trapezius.note: Upper traps recruited heavily by deadlifts, rows, shrugs; mid-traps by rowing patterns.

mid-back.note: Rhomboids and mid-trapezius; tracked as part of horizontal pulling volume.

spinal erectors.note: High systemic fatigue contribution; conservative MRV. Axial loading is limiting factor.

rectus abdominis.note: Significant isometric volume from compound lifts; direct work supplementary.

gastrocnemius.note: Calves respond to high volume; trained heavily in standing calf raises.

soleus.note: Seated calf raises; similar volume tolerance to gastrocnemius.
